members.name: Sofia Chen
members.backstory: Sofia ran the community garden behind the church — forty plots, a hundred neighbors, every weed known by name. She talks to plants. The plants here listen stranger than most. Her grandparents came from Anchorage; she grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than she can say. Knows Latin names for everything. The plants don't care.

members.name: Giulia Bianchi
members.backstory: Giulia is here. Her parents came from Buenos Aires; she grew up hearing Spanish at home, and still understand more than she can say. Stops traffic that isn't there. The children cross anyway, safely, which is the point.

members.name: Adaeze Nwosu
members.backstory: Adaeze taught English to newcomers — patient, gesturing, endlessly rephrasing. In a clearing full of strangers who don't share words, she is suddenly the most important person alive. She learned Spanish on the job as an eSL teacher. She learned Mandarin on the job as an eSL teacher. She learned English on the job as an eSL teacher. Youngest teacher. The kids adore her. She's terrified.

members.name: Nina Petrova
members.backstory: Nina fixed diesel engines. Her hands know the shape of every bolt ever made. Nothing here has bolts. She is learning the shape of everything else. Her parents came from Buenos Aires; she grew up hearing Spanish at home, and still understand more than she can say. Fixes what can't be fixed. Morale is a machine too.

beats.text: A woman, maybe 30s, with a slouched posture spends the afternoon with the tall sunflower-like stalks with knobby tubers at the base, found in sunny patches — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Edible, but it argues on the way down. The fire's verdict: food, carefully. Small amounts.
★ IDENTIFIED: Jerusalem Artichoke. Tall sunflower stalks; dig at the base for knobby tubers. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
